reasoning.Student A:
My personal preference is y > z > w > x. My priority at each school is w: 1, x: 2, y: 1, z: 2. Most applicants favor y > x > w > z.

My top choice is y, and I have priority 1 there. Given that most applicants also favor y, I'm likely to get into y.

My second choice is z, and I have priority 2 there. If I don't get into y (unlikely, but possible), I will automatically be considered at z.

My third choice is w, and I have priority 1 there. If I don't get into y or z, I will automatically be considered at w. Since I have priority 1 at w, and most applicants prefer x > w > z, I have a good chance of getting into w if I am considered there.

My last choice is x, and I have priority 2 there. If I don't get into y, z, or w, I will automatically be considered at x.

Therefore, my ranking should remain the same as my preference.
reasoning.Student B:
My goal is to be matched with the best school possible according to my preferences: z > y > w > x. I also know my priority rank at each school: w: 2, x: 1, y: 2, z: 1. Most applicants prefer y > x > w > z.

School z is my top choice and I have the highest priority (rank 1) there. This makes it very likely I will be matched to z if I apply.

School y is my second choice, and I have priority rank 2 there. Since most applicants prefer y, there will be competition for y. However, my lower priority rank makes it less likely I'll be matched to y if I apply.

School w is my third choice, and I have priority rank 2 there. Since most applicants seem to dislike z, w, and x, it is less competitive than y.

School x is my last choice, but I have the highest priority (rank 1) there. However, I would only want to go to x if I am rejected from all other schools.

Given that I will be automatically considered at all remaining schools on my list if I am rejected from a school, I should rank the schools in order of my preference. This is because if I am rejected from my top choice, I am automatically considered at my second choice, and so on. This strategy maximizes my chances of getting into the best school possible.
